# Turn your Zoom call into meeting minutes in 5 minutes with Grok

You just finished a Zoom call and need minutes fast. Instead of typing for half an hour, you can get help from Grok to create a concise summary. Here's how.

## Before you start
- A **Zoom cloud recording with an audio transcript** — or your own notes from the call. Zoom's help center says audio transcription needs a Pro, Business, Education, or Enterprise account with cloud recording and audio transcription turned on, so switch it on before the meeting.
- A **Grok account** — xAI says you can sign in with your X account or email, and Grok is free to try.
- A **computer or phone** with a web browser.
- Roughly **5 minutes** of your time.
- A **text editor** or email app to paste the minutes.
- **Permission to share the content:** check that your company's rules allow pasting meeting notes into an AI tool, and leave out anything confidential.

> Grok can't send the minutes for you — you'll copy and share them yourself.

## Step 1 — Get your Zoom transcript or notes
Sign in to the Zoom web portal, select **Recordings & Transcripts** in the navigation menu, open the **Cloud recordings** tab, and click the name of your meeting. Zoom saves the audio transcript as a separate **VTT** file in the list of that meeting's recording files — download it. A VTT file opens in any text editor.
If there is no transcript — for example because transcription was off during the call — play the recording and write down the key points yourself, then use those notes in the next step.
You'll know it worked when you have a text file or written notes with the key points from the call.

💬 Example:
Open "Team Sync" in **Recordings & Transcripts** and download its transcript file.

## Step 2 — Open Grok and start a new conversation
Go to [grok.com](https://grok.com) in your browser or open the Grok app, and sign in with your X account or email. Start a fresh conversation, so the minutes don't mix with an earlier chat.
You'll know it worked when you see an empty text box ready for your prompt.

💬 Example:
Type nothing yet — just leave the conversation empty for the next step.

## Step 3 — Ask Grok to write minutes from your notes or transcript
If you have a Zoom transcript file: open it, copy the text, and paste it into Grok's text box.
If you took your own notes: paste those instead.
Then type your prompt:

💬 Example:
"Please write concise meeting minutes from these notes. Include key decisions, action items with owners, and next steps. Keep it under 200 words."

After you send the prompt, Grok writes the minutes below it.
If nothing happens, refresh the page and send it again.
You'll know it worked when Grok displays a formatted set of minutes.

## Step 4 — Review and polish the minutes
When Grok finishes, read the minutes it generated and compare them with your transcript or notes — especially names, numbers, and deadlines. If anything is missing or unclear, reply in the same conversation.
After you send the follow-up, Grok revises the text and shows the new version.
If Grok doesn't change the text, try rephrasing your request ("Include the project name and deadline in the minutes.").
You'll know it worked when the updated minutes appear in the conversation.

💬 Example:
"Add the name of the project we discussed and the deadline for the next milestone."

## Step 5 — Copy and share the minutes
Highlight the minutes text in the conversation, press **Cmd+C** (Mac) or **Ctrl+C** (Windows), and paste them into your email, Slack, or document. Add a subject line like "Minutes from 5 June sync" and send.
If the text doesn't copy, try selecting it again or right-clicking and choosing Copy.
You'll know it worked when the minutes appear in your email or chat app exactly as you pasted them.

💬 Example:
Subject: Minutes from 5 June sync
Body: Please find the minutes below.

---

## Common mistakes
- **Mistake:** Pasting too little information for Grok to work with.
  **Fix:** Include your full notes or transcript — the more context Grok has, the better the minutes.

- **Mistake:** Asking Grok to write minutes without specifying the format.
  **Fix:** Always include "key decisions, action items with owners, and next steps" in your prompt so the output is useful.

- **Mistake:** Sharing the minutes without checking them.
  **Fix:** Compare names, numbers, and deadlines with the transcript, then ask Grok to add anything missing — it's faster than rewriting yourself.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** After any quick catch-up, turn your notes into minutes in minutes instead of typing for half an hour.
- **For your business or work:** Share clear, concise notes with your team right after the call, so everyone knows what to do next.
- **If you're just getting started:** Start with one call this week and see how much time you save.

## Try it now
Open **Recordings & Transcripts** in the Zoom web portal, get your transcript or notes, and paste them into Grok. Ask it to write concise minutes — you'll have the first draft in under two minutes.
